solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Two Biblical characters in a Coleridge poem

parts.note: Christ is the central figure of the New Testament
Abel is the son of Adam killed by Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: A reader spots a pair of figures from Scripture turning up in one of Coleridge's verses.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge wrote an unfinished Gothic narrative poem with this title, named after its heroine.

clue.text: Find rupees in sofa in squat

indicators.note: in shows the abbreviation for the currency sits inside the furniture word

parts.note: a couch is a sofa
R is the abbreviation for rupee or rupees

explanation.surface: Someone finds money down the back of the sofa in a squat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squat' looks like a noun for an occupied building; it is the verb, meaning to hunker down.
explanation.definitionFit: To crouch is to squat down with bent knees close to the ground.

clue.text: Embarrassed top MP

parts.note: embarrassed people go red
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: A senior Member of Parliament is left red-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: MP here is military police, not a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from their red caps.

clue.text: Sit in a pub with a gin, possibly, and agree on terms

parts.note: a sit-in is a form of strike
a bar is a pub

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters are a rearranged version of the words before it

explanation.surface: Two people settle a deal over a gin while sitting in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike a bargain is an idiom for reaching an agreement on a deal.

clue.text: Support services provided by a fellow on newly-built terrace

indicators.note: newly-built implies the letters of the housing word are put together afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A man supplies care on a freshly constructed row of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftercare is support given to patients or clients after treatment or a stay ends.

clue.text: Strangely frightening in middle of Great Lake

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of the word Great

parts.note: Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Something spooky lurks in the centre of one of the Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie describes something weird and unsettling, frightening in an uncanny way.

clue.text: A filter shortened? That's ridiculous

indicators.note: shortened tells us to cut the final letter off the synonym for the filtering word

parts.note: to filter is to sift

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of trimming a filter down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' drops the last letter of SIFT, leaving SIF.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'as if!' is a dismissive retort meaning the idea is absurd.

clue.text: Assistant in kitchen, very good American, leading one astray

parts.note: 'just so' is an old phrase of approval, so 'so' can stand for very good

indicators.note: astray says that something has wandered off, here the one from the chief

parts.note: the leading one is the chief
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A fine American kitchen helper misleads a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' removes I (one) from CHIEF, leaving CHEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A sous-chef is the second-in-command in a professional kitchen, the head chef's assistant.

clue.text: Honesty of food shop shown in appropriate ending of controversy

indicators.note: shown in puts the shop inside the word for appropriate

parts.note: fit means appropriate or suitable
a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

indicators.note: ending of takes the last letter of controversy

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over how honest a food shop is.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidelity is faithfulness and truthfulness, close to honesty.

clue.text: Composers getting out of it

definitions.meaning: the rhyming-slang phrase means drunk, rhyming with a vulgar word for drunk

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it; this pair of composers stands for a coarse British word for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Two Romantic composers, and in rhyming slang a phrase meaning heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Discipline in class

definitions.meaning: keeping discipline is keeping things under control
in biology a class sits above a family and below a phylum, as a rank or grouping

explanation.definitionFit: Order means both orderly control and a taxonomic rank or social grade.

clue.text: Face the other way in stage act, initially

indicators.note: initially says the word for act is placed first, before the word for stage

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act in a variety show
a round is a stage of a competition

explanation.surface: A director tells a performer to turn their back during the opening of a stage routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'stage act', but the pieces come in reverse order: 'initially' puts the act first.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn round is to rotate the body so as to face in the opposite direction.

clue.text: Fine example of a firework

definitions.meaning: informal British praise for something excellent
a small explosive firework that bangs

explanation.definitionFit: Cracker is British slang for a superb specimen and also a type of banging firework.

clue.text: Decent chalet, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect, as an adjective meaning dodgy, signals that the letters are not in their true order

explanation.surface: Someone hedges a judgement that a holiday chalet is respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' looks like a hedge, but I is part of the anagram fodder with CHALET.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical behaviour is morally sound, which is what decent conduct is.

clue.text: Stability shown by these, surprisingly, in financial document

parts.note: balance is steadiness or stability

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the letters of the word that follows land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An accountant notes that the steadiness of a business shows up in its accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance sheet is a statement of a company's assets and liabilities, a standard accounting report.

clue.text: Before work, traces out sled track

indicators.note: Before places the rearranged letters ahead of the word for work
out signals that the letters of traces are put out of their usual order

parts.note: to run a machine is to work it

explanation.surface: A tracker sets off ahead of a job, following signs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cresta Run is a famous ice toboggan track at St Moritz in Switzerland.

clue.text: Rampant male featured in piece I'd prepared

indicators.note: featured in puts the male abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
prepared means made ready, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A rampant man appears in a piece someone has got ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rampant' looks like a description of the male, but it is the definition, used as an adjective for something spreading unchecked; 'prepared' signals the anagram and 'featured in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidemic as an adjective means widespread and rapidly spreading, like rampant disease.

clue.text: Drive from top of drive to one's gatehouse

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of drive in a down clue

parts.note: one's is read as 'one is', and I is one, giving I'S
a lodge is a gatehouse at the entrance to an estate

explanation.surface: Someone travels from the head of an estate driveway down to the gatehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge is to force out or drive something from its place.

clue.text: Secret aims to make money from investments

parts.note: private means secret or not public
means are aims or methods, as in 'means to an end'

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their plans for getting rich to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Private means is an income from investments or inheritance rather than earned wages.

clue.text: Small opening I reportedly must have allowed

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the letter is replaced by a word that sounds the same

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Someone admits they permitted a small gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter I sounds the same as EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small hole for a lace or cord, a tiny opening.

clue.text: Ring wife being entertained by eccentric playwright

indicators.note: being entertained by puts the ring and wife inside the eccentric

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
a ring is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A dramatist hosts an odd friend's ring-wearing wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward was an English playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward was a celebrated English playwright, author of Private Lives.

clue.text: Retiring journalist's cheerful charm

indicators.note: retiring, as in drawing back, tells us to read the newspaper man backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
light, as in light-hearted, means cheerful

explanation.surface: A newspaperman heading for retirement has a sunny, winning personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like an adjective for a shy journalist; here it means going backwards, and 'cheerful' is the light of light-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight someone is to charm or enchant them; both are verbs of giving pleasure.

clue.text: Name lieutenant knocked over in match

indicators.note: in shows that the reversed abbreviation goes inside the word for match

parts.note: a tie is a match or fixture in a cup competition

indicators.note: knocked over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the abbreviation reads upwards

explanation.surface: An army officer is bowled over during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a name, as of a book or a person's rank.

clue.text: Sporting cry made by supporter in front of house after end of contest

indicators.note: after places the next pieces behind that final letter
in front of puts the supporter before the house
end of picks out the final letter of the word contest

parts.note: an ally is someone who supports you

explanation.surface: A fan yells something as a sporting contest finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The cry is the one raised by fox hunters on sighting the quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the traditional shout of the hunt when the fox is seen, a cry of a field sport.

clue.text: Time wind swirls — middle of March, height of season

indicators.note: swirls, as the wind does, suggests these letters are whirled into a new order
middle of takes the central letter of March

explanation.surface: Gusts blow about in mid-March, the peak of the stormy season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' looks like the definition but is fodder: TIME and WIND are rearranged into MIDWINTE, and 'middle of' adds R from March.
explanation.definitionFit: Midwinter is the depth or peak of the winter season, around the solstice.

clue.text: Dance in rehearsal, samba

indicators.note: in shows that the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Dancers practise a Brazilian samba during a rehearsal.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance.

clue.text: Gang boasted

definitions.meaning: a gang is a group of workers or companions
crowed, an old past tense of crow meaning bragged

explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a team or gang, and crew is also an archaic past tense of crow, to brag.

clue.text: Put back in check, say, by daughter

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A daughter is told to restrain herself and is returned to her place.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone to a former position, to put them back there.
